newsitem.title: USA: U.S. raises question on Yeltsin summit date.
newsitem.headline: U.S. raises question on Yeltsin summit date.

text.p: The White House said on Monday it expected a summit between President Bill Clinton and ailing Russian President Boris Yeltsin this year but suggested that the previously agreed time of March may be open to question.

The White House said in December that Clinton and Yeltsin, who underwent quintuple heart bypass surgery last year and is now recovering from pneumonia, had agreed to meet in March but had not set an exact date or venue.
"We'll see as we continue to work through with the Russian government...whether that still suggests itself as a time," White House spokesman Mike McCurry told reporters.
McCurry, at his daily briefing, said he expected the matter to be discussed when Vice President Al Gore and Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomydrin hold a scheduled Feb. 6-8 meeting in Washington.
"We have not set a time or place for the meeting that we expect to occur later this year between President Yeltsin and President Clinton," McCurry added.
Yeltsin on Monday cancelled plans to visit the Netherlands on his doctors' orders, deepening concern about his health and raising doubts in Russia about his ability to govern.
